audit_findings.title: Post-2025 financing costs may be absent while its cash proceeds are added
audit_findings.magnitude: $664.4 million net 2026 financing cash contribution, computed as $1,129.3 million note proceeds less $69.0 million capped-call payment and $440.5 million conversion payment plus $44.6 million hedge-and-warrant proceeds; 23.8% of $2,794.0 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds June 2026 cash, while the OE anchor is derived entirely from 2016-2025 results and therefore cannot contain the post-2025 financing's issuance-cost amortization, settlement economics or other recurring consequences.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, our only outstanding debt is the $575.0 million Convertible Notes, which mature on September 15, 2028 and carry a 2.5% interest rate.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated, although the resulting overstatement is not yet fully measured. The 2031 Notes have a 0% coupon, so omitted cash interest is not demonstrated, but the bridge includes a material financing-derived cash increase without deducting principal under the stipulated equity-OE method. Dilution and conversion settlements may partly offset this elsewhere, but the amount involved is large enough to change intrinsic value materially.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $1.15 billion 2031 Notes and remaining 2028 Notes through net proceeds, capped call, exchanges, redemption and retained cash; then rerun using a single consistent financing state that includes all associated OE costs, cash settlement and dilution.

audit_findings.title: Terminal OE may perpetuate an expiring tax holiday
audit_findings.magnitude: $31.0 million 2025 tax-holiday benefit, equal to 31.2% of the $99.5 million OE anchor; separate $9.8 million 2025 valuation-allowance release
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated cash-tax burden inflates normalized OE and, if carried through the forecast and terminal value, overstates operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: This tax holiday is in effect through June 30, 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 30, 2027 expiration and the $31.0 million 2025 benefit are filed facts. That benefit is large relative to the anchor, and the terminal value is about half of scenario value. It is unresolved how much of the benefit remains embedded in the log-trend anchor, while Pillar II was already partly present in 2025. Failure to normalize the expiring holiday and discrete $9.8 million release could therefore materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct normalized cash taxes for every OE year, remove discrete valuation-allowance effects, estimate the post-June-2027 Singapore rate and Pillar II burden, and rerun all scenarios with the normalized OE series.

audit_findings.title: Convertible dilution and the OE numerator may represent different capital structures
audit_findings.magnitude: 6.195532 million excess valuation shares over the 40.050442 million shares outstanding on July 29, 2026, or 15.5%; denominator-only base value would be approximately $69.76 per share instead of $60.42, a $9.34 per-share difference
audit_findings.mechanism: The assumed conversion state changes fully diluted shares, retained interest expense, available cash, principal settlement and the economic effects of note hedges, warrants and the capped call.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon conversion, we have the option to pay or deliver, as the case may be, cash, shares of our common stock, or a combination of cash and shares of our common stock with respect to the remainder, if any, of our conversion obligation in excess of the aggregate principal amount of the Convertible Notes being converted.
audit_findings.explanation: A material numerator-denominator mismatch is demonstrated: the valuation uses 46.245974 million shares while the filed outstanding count is 40.050442 million, and it retains debt-capital-structure OE and cash. Maximum dilution can understate per-share value, while failure to recognize conversion cash settlement or financing claims can overstate it; the net direction therefore cannot be determined without a consistent instrument-by-instrument model.
audit_findings.action: Model the 2028 Notes, 2031 Notes, warrants, note hedges and capped call separately under outstanding-debt and assumed-conversion states; update interest, settlement cash and incremental shares together, then rerun the bridge and per-share values.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded pension obligations may be an unbridged senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $51.6 million pension deficit, equal to 1.85% of $2,794.0 million base equity value and $1.12 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any past-service pension deficit not already captured through OE contributions would reduce the equity bridge as a senior claim.
audit_findings.evidence: We currently have unfunded obligations to our pension plans.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether OE used employer contributions or accounting pension expense remains unresolved, but deducting the entire filed deficit would reduce base value only from $60.42 to approximately $59.30 per share and bull value from $65.85 to approximately $64.73. That scale cannot change the valuation conclusion relative to the $280.90 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the OE treatment of the filed $1.7 million 2025 employer contributions and pension expense; if inconsistent, deduct the residual $51.6 million deficit or substitute a contribution-based OE adjustment.

audit_findings.title: Discontinued inverter operations still create recurring cash costs
audit_findings.magnitude: Discontinued-operation operating cash outflows of $4.0 million in 2023, $2.2 million in 2024, $1.4 million in 2025 and $1.0 million for first-half 2026; annualizing first-half 2026 and capitalizing at 7.5% gives $26.7 million, or $0.58 per diluted share and 1.0% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If excluded from the OE series, continuing warranty, maintenance, repair and run-off cash payments should reduce OE until the obligations expire.
audit_findings.evidence: We plan to continue supporting inverter customers with service maintenance and repair operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring cash drain is demonstrated, while its exclusion from OE and the magnitude of future litigation or warranty overruns remain unresolved. At the current filed run rate, even a conservative perpetuity treatment is about 1% of base equity value and cannot change the valuation conclusion. Larger litigation or warranty losses are unquantified possibilities rather than demonstrated valuation errors.
audit_findings.action: Verify whether discontinued-operation cash outflows were included in each OE year and obtain the inverter-specific warranty reserve, service-contract forecast and litigation exposure; rerun a finite run-off schedule if they were excluded.
